subject: Archive search request — Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, Cardiff — December 1988 (personal research)
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text: Dear ITV Viewers Requests,  Further search terms for my email of 10 October 2026, “Archive search request - Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, Cardiff - December 1988 (personal research)”  I am following up on that request after ITV Clipsales advised that personal and academic research enquiries should be sent to this address. New information has come to light about historical farm, estate and locality nomenclature, including the 1881 census wording “Llandough Home Farm”. Please associate the terms below with my existing request and rerun or extend the relevant archive checks for the regional or national news coverage filmed or transmitted in late November and December 1988 concerning the farmhouse possession or demolition and adjoining site. The original request’s subject and period remain unchanged.  The intended site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr beside St Dochdwy’s Church at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, near Penarth and Cardiff, Vale of Glamorgan. Please use the site identifiers as the primary means of disambiguation: Heneb/GGAT HER GGAT02038s; RCAHMW NPRN 20182; grid reference ST16707335; and the later development address Church View Close, [postcode redacted]. The relevant mapping references are County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW, including 38-1-608 and 38-1-334. The approximate reference in my original email was ST 168 733.  Farm and farmhouse search forms  Please consider “Great House Farm”; “Great House Farm, Llandough”; “Great House Farm (GGAT02038s)”; “Great House”; “Great house”; “Greathouse”; “Tŷ Mawr”; “Ty Mawr”; “Ty-mawr”; “Ty Mawr Farm”; “Ty Mawr (Great House)”; “Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Cydfin Farm”; “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”; “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”; “Cedfin”; “Cydwin”; “Cedwyn”; “Cedfyn”; “Cefin”; “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm”; “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm”; “Llandough Church Farm”; “Church Farm”; “former Great House Farm”; “a 3.4 acre site located adjacent St. Dochdwy Parish Church”; and “LLANDOUGH FARM (Ideal Homes Wales)”. “Ty-mawr” is also recorded on an Ordnance Survey 25-inch map, although the edition and its precise relationship to the site have not been confirmed.  These are candidate search strings, not interchangeable names or proof that each record concerns the same building, parcel or holding. The checked 1881 census image reads “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm” is a reported competing transcription. The checked page does not contain “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm”. “Cydwin” and “Cedwyn” are reported research leads whose underlying 16th-century documents have not been verified; “Cedfyn” and “Cefin” are retained as search forms without a confirmed primary occurrence. “Llandough Church Farm” and “Church Farm” are source-specific terms whose connection to this site is not established. The Bute catalogue lists “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)” within a 1552 - 1824 catalogue range, which is not a specific date for that wording. The 1824 Stewart survey, plan 19, records “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” (Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1). “LLANDOUGH FARM” appears on the 1994 Ideal Homes Wales plan for the development site, but other records use Llandough Farm for a separate farmstead; please distinguish by mapped location.  Wider estate search forms  For relevant records about the surrounding area, please also consider “Cedwyn Estate”, “Cydwin”, “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”, “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” and “Cwm Cydfin Wood”. “Cedwyn Estate” is the family’s working name for the wider historic estate, not a period name established by the records cited here. “Cydwin” is a reported lead from a 1547 family research note whose underlying document is not held. “Cwm Cydfin Wood” appears in a 1902 Bute sale catalogue. These are search aids for relevant site and surrounding-area records; they do not establish that all terms denote the same holding or prove the estate’s extent or title.  Locality and administrative search forms  Please also consider “Llandough-juxta-Penarth”; “Llandough near Penarth”; “Llandough near Cardiff”; “Llandough, Penarth”; “Llandough, Cardiff”; “Llandough”; “Landoche-juxta-Cardif”; “Llandough / Leckwith”; “Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Urban District of Penarth”; “Llandochau”; “CF64”; and “Church View Close, [postcode redacted]”. “Landoche-juxta-Cardif” is a historical locator for the manor, not proof that every holding recorded under it is this farm. “Llandough / Leckwith” is neighbouring parish and manorial context, not another name for the farm. The locality forms are aids to retrieval and should be kept separate from the farm and estate names. Llandough near Cowbridge and Llandow are outside the scope of this request and should be excluded as false matches.  Please record which terms and archive indexes or catalogues were checked, and tell me whether any relevant item, production record or alternative custodian was newly identified. If this inbox is limited to supplying copies rather than archive searches, please direct this supplement to the appropriate ITV archive contact or let me know the correct route.  The nomenclature references and fuller notes are available at: https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nomenclature/c/great-house-farm/ https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nomenclature/c/cedwyn-estate/ https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nomenclature/c/llandough/ https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/wiki/great-house-farm/name-variations/ https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/wiki/great-house-farm/location-name-nomenclature/  Yours faithfully,  Requester   https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate
